items.summary: Accessible inputs and actions with controlled state and StyleX styling.
useWhen: Collecting user input or invoking an application-owned action
avoidWhen: The application cannot implement the visible action or own the controlled value
sideEffects: Invokes controlled value and action callbacks supplied by the application
accessibility: Native controls retain keyboard and form semantics
Labels, descriptions, validation, and icon-only actions have accessible names
examples: Render a controlled TextField with an associated label and validation message
nonExamples: Render an enabled action without an observable application callback

items.summary: Semantic progress and status feedback with reduced-motion behavior.
useWhen: Communicating coarse progress or a user-relevant operation state
avoidWhen: Repeating lifecycle feedback already announced by the owning region
accessibility: Status text remains available without relying on color or motion
examples: Render determinate Progress with a visible label and current value
nonExamples: Mount a second live spinner for an operation already represented by its parent

items.summary: Accessible modal and disclosure surfaces with managed focus and state.
useWhen: Revealing secondary content or requiring focused modal interaction
avoidWhen: Permanent page content can remain visible in the normal reading flow
sideEffects: Dialog moves focus into the modal surface and restores it on close
accessibility: Dialog traps focus and supports Escape
Disclosure exposes expanded state through its native trigger
examples: Use Dialog for a reversible confirmation with an explicit close path
nonExamples: Open a modal without a title, description, or focus restoration

items.summary: Coordinates bounded enter, exit, layout, state, and text transitions without owning application state.
useWhen: A component needs identity-preserving presence or state transition behavior
avoidWhen: Immediate state replacement is clearer or the interaction is too frequent to animate
sideEffects: Coordinates mounted presence and transition completion callbacks
accessibility: Accessible state updates are not delayed by visual transitions
examples: Use StateTransition to preserve identity while a visible lifecycle label changes
nonExamples: Animate a high-frequency keyboard action or delay semantic state until animation completes

items.summary: Screen-reader text without visual layout changes.
useWhen: Visible content does not provide the accessible text required by its context
avoidWhen: The same text should remain visible to every user
actions: provide an accessible name or description
accessibility: Text remains in the accessibility tree without affecting visual layout
examples: Name an icon-only control when no visible label is appropriate
nonExamples: Hide instructions that sighted keyboard users also need
